title: Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026 Passed
shortDescription: Gujarat becomes the second Indian state after Uttarakhand to enact a Uniform Civil Code, following a report by a committee headed by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai.
genZNote: Second state, same script as Uttarakhand — but the exam only cares that you know WHICH state was first and WHICH group got exempted.

sections.heading: What Happened
sections.body: On 24–25 March 2026, the Gujarat Legislative Assembly passed the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill, 2026 by voice vote after a debate lasting more than seven hours, with the opposition Congress and AAP withholding support. The bill was tabled by Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel on the recommendation of a committee headed by retired Supreme Court Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, which had collected over 20 lakh public suggestions before submitting its report in March 2026.

sections.heading: Key Facts
bullets: Gujarat is the SECOND state in India to enact a UCC, after Uttarakhand (which passed its UCC in February 2024).
The law creates one common legal framework for marriage, divorce, succession, adoption, and live-in relationships, applying irrespective of religion.
Marriages must be registered within 60 days; live-in relationships within 30 days — failure to register a marriage draws a penalty (reported up to ₹10,000), though the marriage itself isn't voided.
Polygamy and bigamy are banned outright, one spouse at a time for everyone.
Scheduled Tribes are explicitly EXEMPTED from the code, to protect their customary personal-law practices.
Deputy CM Harsh Sanghavi piloted the bill's defence in the Assembly alongside CM Patel.

sections.heading: Why It Matters
sections.body: Article 44 of the Constitution directs the state to work toward a Uniform Civil Code as a Directive Principle — Gujarat's UCC is presented by the state government as a step toward that goal, and connects directly to the Constitution of India's DPSP chapter. It's also a live example of Centre-state and constitutional-bodies topics (a state exercising its legislative competence over personal law) intersecting with current, real-world implementation.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Gujarat passed its own Uniform Civil Code Bill in March 2026, becoming the second state after Uttarakhand to do so.
keyFacts: Passed 24–25 March 2026 by voice vote after a 7+ hour debate.
Committee headed by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai recommended the code.
Scheduled Tribes are exempted from the code.
commonConfusion: Uttarakhand was first (2024), Gujarat is second (2026) — don't swap the order in an MCQ.

highYieldFacts: The Desai Committee's recommendations formed the basis of Gujarat's bill.
Scheduled Tribes are exempted from the code's application.
commonTraps: Assuming Gujarat was the first state to pass a UCC — it was second.
Assuming the UCC applies uniformly to every community in Gujarat without exception — Scheduled Tribes are carved out.
mustRemember: Gujarat UCC, 2026 — passed 24–25 March 2026, second state after Uttarakhand, ST-exempted.
